read.thesis: Deutsche Telekom raised FY26 EBITDA to ~EUR47.6bn and FCF to ~EUR20.1bn, passing through T-Mobile's upgrade; German broadband turned positive at +11% on churn and fiber, with no supply-side capex cut and a flat EUR2bn FY27 buyback.

capex.peers_comment: Competitors are slowing fiber rollout; DT keeps pace and expanded fiber investment envelope.
capex.quote: we are accelerating the fiber connections while our competition is significantly slowing down

triggers.label: Competitors slowing fiber rollout
triggers.quote: we are accelerating the fiber connections while our competition is significantly slowing down

triggers.label: Broadband revenue growth 2.8%
triggers.quote: Broadband revenue growth accelerated to 2.8%, supported, a, by the stabilization of the customer base

triggers.label: FY26 EBITDA raised to EUR47.6bn
triggers.quote: our '26, group EBITDA will be around EUR47.6 billion, and our group free cash flow guidance will increase to around EUR20.1

triggers.label: Rivals not following price rises
triggers.quote: Now I cannot say that AT&T and Verizon are following us.

our group free cash flow guidance will increase to around EUR20.1
Our guidance for adjusted EPS will be at the EUR2.20.
we are still in reach to reach the lower end of the guidance of 2.5% to 3% for the year '26

red_flags.label: Mobile price competition from MVNOs and Vodafone
red_flags.quote: we have seen some price competition, especially here with Vodafone. So therefore, the growth hasn't been that strong.

red_flags.label: Component price inflation in fiber and CPE
red_flags.quote: Obviously, we're facing component price inflation.

red_flags.quote: probably the total volume which we're going to buy back is somewhere in the vicinity of EUR3 billion to EUR3.5 billion. So we're going to be short
